page.layout: One printed page: one column of running text; marginal notes in the left margin ("Sacerdotes.", "Levitæ."); a catchword at the lower right. A strip of the neighbouring page at the right edge is not transcribed.

main_text.p: esse David voluit. Personas igitur sacras distri-buit, ut per singula Sabbatha vices suas, quas sorte obtinuerant, implerent. Fueruntque vices o-mnibus, & seorsim, & conjunctim designatæ, vi-gintiquatuor, in quas totum sacerdotum colle-gium sorte distributum erat. Non omnes ergo Levitæ assiduè Hierosolymis agere tenebantur, sed quælibet sacerdotum classis, cum sua Levita-rum turma die Sabbathi ad ministrandum ingre-diebatur templum; eodem die sors illa, quæ offi-cium suum elapsâ septimanâ obierat, egredieba-tur, & ad suas singuli civitates, quarum quadra-ginta octo per totam terram Chanaan occupa-bant, revertebatur, in Synagogis per singula Sab-batha, in erudiendis adultis & pueris officium suum facientes.

Divisit ergo David personas sacras omnes, Sacerdotes. primò in Sacerdotes & Levitas. Sacerdotum officium erat præcipuum, docere, benedicere, sacri-ficare, & adolere odores, per quos preces san-ctorum significabantur.

Levitæ. Levitæ, quorum 24000 numerati fuerunt, veluti diaconi, destinati erant sacerdotum mini-sterio, in atriis administrando, quæ ibi agenda e-rant, in cubiculis, in sacrorum vasorum emun-datione, in excoriandis pecudibus, ablutione hostiarum, apponendis & ordinandis singulis Sabbathis panibus propositionis, apparandis fi-milâ, laganis infermentatis, frixis vel toftis, asser-vandis, depromendis & mundandis vasis sacris, & quæ his erant similia. Levitas iterum in Doc-tores, Musicos, Janitores, Thesaurarios & Præfe-

page.notes: The catchword "ctos" is read as the start of "Præfectos" printed at the foot; [?] is not added because the letters are clear, but the form may be doubtful. The text ends on the broken word "Præfe-" as printed. The long s has been written as plain s throughout, including where the scan shows an f-like form (e.g. "fuum", "fingula", "vafis"). Two readings of hyphen breaks follow the printed line ends.
